audit.why: 47.9% Emerald+ over 44 real games and TRICKY at 7/10 is a fair read on a genuine AP mirror: Sylas out-trades levels 2-3 on Chain Lash and Kingslayer sustain, the lane levels off once Nether Blade and Riftwalk exist, and Hijack keeps the late game a coin-flip rather than a Kassadin free win.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three stages contradict their own captions. win[1] said Skill while whys[1] ends 'he out-trades me here'. win[4] said Sylas while whys[4] says Riftwalk is 'neutralizing his all-in and pulling us level'. win[6] said Kassadin while whys[6] says Hijack keeps it 'a true coin-flip'. full.phases carried the same three.
audit.why: The Level 6 row is the one place Kassadin genuinely draws even in this matchup, and it was labelled a Sylas win; meanwhile Two+ items was labelled a Kassadin win by a caption that explicitly refuses to call it one.
audit.corrected: Level 2 to Sylas, Level 6 to Skill, Two+ items to Skill, on win[] and phases[].side. Levels 1, 3, 4-5 and First item are unchanged.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (a) The full layer describes Abscond / Abduct as a 'Dash into chain-stun' in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t. Riot's text has no stun: 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits.' (b) The content layer has the pull backwards — early says 'his E grab can pull me into the combo' and wants.foe[0] says 'Land his E (Abduct) grab to pull you into a point-blank Q+W combo'. Abduct pulls Sylas to you, not you to Sylas. That matters because the counterplay is different: you dodge the chain or step out of where he will arrive, and there is no displacement on you to plan around.
audit.why: Riot's own wording is unambiguous on both counts, and a laner who believes they are about to be displaced will play the wrong reaction.
audit.corrected: 'Chain-stun' is gone; the ability is now described as a dash plus a chain-pull that brings him to you. Fixed in early, whys[2], wants.foe[0], enemyWin, dosFull[0], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' and it was correct — 'bait his E and W cooldowns' and 'punish him hard while it is down' appear repeatedly with no number attached, and 'never Riftwalk while his R is up' never says how long up lasts.
audit.why: Abscond / Abduct is 13/12/11/10/9s, Kingslayer 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s and Hijack 80/55/30s. The Hijack number changes behaviour most: at rank 1 an 80-second cooldown means most of the game is safe to blink in, while at rank 3 it is 30 seconds and effectively always up.
audit.corrected: 13s for E, 12s for W and 80s-down-to-30s for Hijack are now in mid, late, winCon, tradeGood, dosFull[0], dosFull[2], breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], report[9] and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: Kingslayer's heal is named as a problem four times and Grievous Wounds is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's Kingslayer text: 'lunges at an enemy with magical force dealing damage and healing himself against enemy champions', on a cooldown that falls to 6 seconds. In an AP mirror Kassadin has to win with repeated short blink-trades, an unchecked 6-second heal undoes the whole pattern, and Morellonomicon sits naturally in his build.
audit.corrected: Morellonomicon named in wants.you[2] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: content early, mid, late and all seven whys are written in the first person — 'we are both weak', 'my Null Sphere', 'I blink', 'my Void Stone passive' — while spikes and wants on the same page use second person. breakdown.late also claims a 'Q-silence'.
audit.why: The house voice is second person, and a page that switches between 'I' and 'you' halfway down reads like two different authors. Null Sphere has no silence.
audit.corrected: All ten first-person fields converted to second person with no other change of meaning; the silence claim replaced with the interrupt.

edits.before: Level 1 we are both weak, but Sylas pulls ahead at 2-3: his Q (Chain Lash) lands a delayed double-detonation for chunky poke, his W (Kingslayer) heals him on every trade, and his E grab can pull me into the combo, while my Null Sphere is a single short-range mana-sink with no Nether Blade sustain yet. Do not throw Q to poke and then sit in his range — last-hit with the Q tip and farm defensively. My Void Stone passive (15% less magic damage) softens his AP a little, but I cannot win a straight trade here, so concede the level and protect my HP.
edits.after: Level 1 you are both weak, but Sylas pulls ahead at 2-3: Chain Lash (Q) lands a delayed double-detonation for chunky poke, Kingslayer (W) heals him on every trade, and Abduct chains him onto you for the follow-up, while your Null Sphere is a single short-range mana-sink with no Nether Blade sustain yet. Do not throw Q to poke and then sit in his range — last-hit with the Q tip and farm defensively. Void Stone's 15% magic reduction softens his AP a little, but you cannot win a straight trade here, so concede the level and protect your HP.

edits.before: Through 4-5 Nether Blade finally restores my mana off champion hits (quintupled vs him), so I stop being mana-starved and can farm under tower without going OOM. At 6 Riftwalk is the equalizer: I blink the instant he commits his E grab or W dash, denying him the Kingslayer-heal trade that beat me earlier. Bait his E and W cooldowns — once his grab and heal are down he has no reliable lock, and I can Null Sphere-shield through his Q and walk away even.
edits.after: Through 4-5 Nether Blade finally restores your mana off champion hits (quintupled against him), so you stop being mana-starved and farm under tower without going dry. At 6 Riftwalk is the equalizer: blink the instant he commits Abscond or the Kingslayer lunge, denying him the heal-trade that beat you earlier. Count them — Abscond / Abduct is 13s at rank 1 and Kingslayer 12s — and once both are down he has no lock and no sustain, so shield through Chain Lash and walk away even.

edits.before: This is a 50/50 AP scaling fight and it stays close, but late is where I tilt it: stacked Riftwalk with Rabadon's and ability haste lets me blink repeatedly onto his squishies, and Void Stone plus my Null Sphere shield blank a real share of his magic burst since Sylas is a pure AP threat. The one rule — never Riftwalk in his face while his R (Hijack) is up, because he steals my ult and turns my own escalating blink against me. Force him to spend R on a teammate first, then dive.
edits.after: This is a 50/50 AP scaling fight and it stays close. Stacked Riftwalk with Rabadon's and ability haste lets you blink repeatedly onto his squishies, and Void Stone plus the Null Sphere shield blank a real share of his burst since Sylas is a pure AP threat. The one rule — never Riftwalk in his face while Hijack is up, because he steals your ult and turns your own escalating blink against you. Hijack is 80s at rank 1 but only 30s maxed, so make him spend it on a teammate first, then dive.

notes: This matchup's content layer was written in the first person ('my Null Sphere', 'I blink the instant he commits') across early, mid, late and all seven whys, while its own spikes and wants used second person. Standing kit-flag misfire as in the other files: kassadin.json tags Null Sphere as a channel and _missing-interactions.json generates rows off that; Riot's description says Null Sphere interrupts channels rather than being one, so none of those rows are on the page.
